Learned Dynamics Models Substantially Improve Control Performance Across Diverse Robotic Domains

C. Vague, D. Underspecified

NOTE: This document is a SYNTHETIC fixture shipped with repro-agent. It is not a
real paper and describes no real experiment by any real author. It exists so the
UNTESTABLE triage path can be demonstrated offline.

Abstract

We demonstrate that learned dynamics models substantially improve control
performance across a diverse suite of robotic manipulation and locomotion
domains. Our approach consistently outperforms strong baselines.

1. Introduction

Learning a model of the environment remains one of the most promising routes to
sample-efficient control. We present an approach that combines several such ideas
and evaluate it broadly.

2. Method

Our architecture consists of an encoder, a latent dynamics module, and a decoder,
trained end-to-end. Hyperparameters were selected by informal search and are
omitted for space. Full details will be released with the code.

3. Experiments

We evaluate on a suite of simulated robotic domains spanning manipulation and
locomotion. Across these domains our method substantially outperforms the
baselines we compare against. Performance is measured by normalized score.

Figure 3 shows the aggregate comparison. Our method's advantage is consistent
across the suite. Exact per-domain numbers, environment versions, and the number
of random seeds are deferred to the appendix, which is not included in this
version.

4. Conclusion

Learned dynamics models substantially improve control performance across diverse
robotic domains.
